newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy seeks extension of Albania force mandate.
newsitem.headline: Italy seeks extension of Albania force mandate.

text.p: Italy said on Tuesday that it had asked the United Nations Security Council to extend the mandate of the international protection force in Albania to cover a limited period after elections set for June 29.
The Rome-based steering committee of the countries participating in the force said in a statement that it had recommended the 6,500-strong, Italian-led force stay on.

"The steering committee has recommended to the U.N. Security Council that the presence of the multinational force continue in Albania, in conformity with resolution 1101, for a limited period," the statement said.
Italian television and news agencies said the extension was expected to cover a 45-day post-election period.
The Italian request was a formality, with Albania's national unity government asking the international community at the weekend to extend the force's mandate by three months.
"It is obvious that the mandate will be extended,", a spokesman for the force, Lieutenant-Colonel Giovanni Bernardi, said last Saturday after the Albania request.
The force, made up of troops from 10 European countries, had been due to move out on June 28, the day before the first round of polling for early parliamentary elections.
The vote is designed to end months of rebellion and banditry triggered by the collapse of fraudulent pyramid savings schemes which bankrupted countless Albanians.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) has said it will send more than 400 observers to Albania to watch the election.
More than 100 experts are already in place, moving about with support from the multinational troops.
